entry: City and county in [[California]] (pop., 2025: 826,079), the second-densest major city in the United States and a global center for technology and finance. Settlers from [[New Spain]] founded the Presidio of San Francisco and the Mission San Francisco de Asís in 1776, both named for Francis of Assisi. The California gold rush of 1849 brought rapid growth, and the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed three-quarters of the city, which was quickly rebuilt. During [[World War II]] it was a major port of embarkation for servicemen shipping out to the Pacific theater. After the war, the Summer of Love and the gay rights movement led to its reputation as a center of liberal activism. Its economy is anchored by leading universities and by high-tech, healthcare, finance and professional services; its 2024 GDP was $268 billion. Landmarks include the [[Golden Gate Bridge]], cable cars and [[Alcatraz Island]].

Capital and largest city of [[Costa Rica]] (pop., 2022: 352,381 in the canton). Founded in 1736 by order of the Cabildo de León to concentrate scattered inhabitants, it was named for Joseph of Nazareth, patron of its first chapel. It had no city government until the Constitution of Cádiz took effect in 1812, and it became the national capital in 1823. It has been Costa Rica's capital three times and remains the seat of national government, the focal point of political and economic activity, and a major transport hub. The first modern urban neighborhood, Barrio Amón, was built in [[Belle Époque]] style in the late 19th century, a legacy of the [[Coffee|coffee]] boom. The city is home to the Museo Nacional de Costa Rica and the National Theater. With Alajuela, Heredia and Cartago it forms a Greater Metropolitan Area of over 2 million people (2017). It was one of the safest cities in the region in 2012 and joined the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities in 2016.

City in California, the most populous in the San Francisco Bay Area and Northern California (pop., 2025: 989,814). Founded in 1777 as the Pueblo de San José de Guadalupe, the first city founded in the Californias, it became the state's first capital after statehood. Its transformation from an agricultural center into a metropolis was driven by the technology industry of [[Silicon Valley]], and its motto, "Capital of Silicon Valley", dates to 1988. Headquarters include [[Cisco]], [[EBay|eBay]], Adobe and [[PayPal]]. The city has one of the world's largest overseas Vietnamese populations and the largest Sikh gurdwara outside India.

Capital and most populous municipality of [[Puerto Rico]], an unincorporated territory of the United States. Founded by Spanish imperialists in 1521 as Ciudad de Puerto Rico, it is the second-oldest European-established capital in the Americas, after [[Santo Domingo]], and the oldest European-established city under U.S. sovereignty. Old San Juan contains Fort San Felipe del Morro, Fort San Cristóbal and La Fortaleza, the oldest executive mansion in continuous use in the Americas. These historic sites were declared a [[World Heritage Site]] by [[UNESCO]] in 1983. Today San Juan is the island's most important seaport and a leading financial, cultural and tourism center. Its metropolitan area has about 2.443 million people, roughly 76% of Puerto Rico's population. The city hosted the 1979 Pan American Games.

Landlocked microstate in Southern Europe, completely surrounded by [[Italy]] (pop., 2025: 34,042). It claims to have been founded in AD 301 by Saint Marinus, a stonemason from the island of Rab, and to be the oldest extant sovereign state and constitutional republic. Its borders have remained unchanged since 1463. Two Captains Regent, chosen from opposing political parties, serve six-month terms as joint heads of state and preside over institutions including the Grand and General Council, the elected legislature. San Marino is a member of the [[Council of Europe]] and uses the euro, but is not part of the [[European Union]]. Its economy rests on finance, industry, services, retail and tourism. It was the first existing state to abolish the death penalty, in 1865.

Capital and largest city of [[El Salvador]] and of its department. It is the country's political, cultural, educational and financial center, and it houses the Legislative Assembly, the Supreme Court and the official residence of the president. The municipality had 525,990 inhabitants in 2024, and its metropolitan area, comprising the capital and 13 municipalities, had 2,404,097. The conquistador Gonzalo de Alvarado founded a mission he named San Salvador in 1525. The town moved twice, in 1528 and 1545, settling in the Valle de Las Hamacas for more space and fertile land near the Acelhuate River. Set in the Salvadoran highlands, the city is surrounded by volcanoes and prone to earthquakes. It hosted the Central American and Caribbean Games in 1935, 2002 and 2023, and the 18th Ibero-American Summit in 2008.

City and municipality in the Basque Country of [[Spain]], also called Donostia and capital of Gipuzkoa province (pop., 2024: 188,487). It lies on the coast of the [[Bay of Biscay]], 20 km (12 miles) from the Spain–France border. Its economy is dominated by commerce and [[Tourism|tourism]]. The San Sebastián International Film Festival and the Jazz Festival give it an international profile. In 2016 it shared the title of European Capital of Culture with [[Wrocław]], Poland. By 1181 the city had been chartered by King Sancho VI of Pamplona.

Indigenous [[Hunter-gatherer|hunter-gatherer]] cultures of southern Africa, also called Saan or Bushmen, and the oldest surviving cultures of the region. Genetic analysis suggests divergence from other humans as early as 100,000 to 200,000 years ago. Their ancestral territories span [[Botswana]], [[Namibia]], Angola, Zambia, [[Zimbabwe]], [[Lesotho]] and [[South Africa]]. Their languages belong to the Khoe, Tuu and Kxʼa families. In 2017 Botswana was home to approximately 63,500 San, the highest proportion of any country at 2.8%; Namibia enumerated 71,201 in 2023, or 2.4%. "San" is a Khoekhoe term adopted by Western anthropologists, and in 2003 representatives stated their preference for their individual nation names. "Bushmen" is now considered pejorative by many South Africans.

Capital and largest city of [[Yemen]], at an elevation of 2,300 m (7,500 ft), the seventh-highest capital in the world. Its population is approximately 3,300,000 (2023). The Kingdom of Saba founded the city in the 1st century CE as a secondary capital, and it was later an important military and trade center on routes linking Ma'rib and the Red Sea. The Old City, a [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Site, is known for multistory buildings decorated with geometric patterns, and the Al-Saleh Mosque, the largest in the country, lies in the southern outskirts. In September 2014 the Houthis captured Sanaa from the government. The internationally recognized government moved its seat to [[Aden]], which was declared the temporary capital in March 2015.

Granular material of finely divided rock and mineral particles, usually defined by grain size. Sand grains range from 0.0625 to 2 mm in diameter, smaller than gravel and coarser than silt. In inland and non-tropical coastal settings its most common constituent is silica (SiO₂), usually as [[Quartz]], which resists weathering. Calcium carbonate dominates in reef areas such as the [[Caribbean]], where it derives from coral and shellfish. Sand is a non-renewable resource over human timescales, and desert sand is unsuitable for [[Concrete|concrete]]; 50 billion tons of beach and fossil sand are used each year for construction.

Shorebird of the family *Scolopacidae*, which includes about 98 extant or recently extinct species, among them sandpipers, woodcocks, curlews and snipes. Sandpipers have long bodies, legs and narrow wings, and most species have sensitive bills that probe mud and sand for small [[Invertebrate|invertebrates]]. They measure 12 to 66 cm (4.7–26.0 in) long and usually have dull brown, grey or streaked plumage. Most species nest in open areas, laying three or four eggs in a simple scrape on the ground. The family was introduced by Constantine Samuel Rafinesque in 1815, and its fossil record extends back into the Paleogene.

American actress and film producer. Her breakthrough in the action thriller *Speed* (1994) led to leading roles in the romantic comedies *While You Were Sleeping* and *Practical Magic*, and later to *Miss Congeniality* (2000). She won the Academy Award for Best Actress for *The Blind Side* (2009) and was nominated for *Gravity* (2013), her highest-grossing live-action film. Named the world's highest-paid actress in 2010 and 2014, she founded the production company Fortis Films.

Italian painter of the Early Renaissance, known for mythological and religious subjects. He lived all his life in one neighborhood of Florence, and his best-known works, *The Birth of Venus* and *Primavera*, are in the [[Uffizi]]. He painted many images of the Madonna and Child, often in round tondo form, and received patronage from the Medici family, including [[Lorenzo de' Medici]]. He worked in Pisa in 1474 and in the [[Sistine Chapel]] in Rome in 1481–82. His reputation declined after his death until the Pre-Raphaelites revived it in the late 19th century. His last works moved toward a more Gothic or "archaic" style, in a direction opposite to that of [[Leonardo da Vinci]].

Clastic sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized grains (0.0625 to 2 mm) cemented together by another mineral. Sandstones make up about 20–25% of all sedimentary rocks. Most are composed of [[Quartz|quartz]] or [[Feldspar|feldspar]], the minerals most resistant to surface weathering. Impurities give sandstone its color, most commonly tan, brown, yellow, red, grey, pink, white or black, and red varieties owe their color to [[Hematite|hematite]]. Porous sandstone can store large quantities of water and petroleum, making it a valuable [[Aquifer|aquifer]] and reservoir. Quartz-bearing sandstone can be changed into quartzite through metamorphism, usually related to tectonic compression.

Dish of a filling such as meat, cheese or vegetables between slices of [[Bread|bread]], or any dish in which bread serves as a wrapper for another food. It began as a portable, convenient food in the Western world and is now prevalent worldwide. It is named after the inventor of a roast-beef sandwich, John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich, an 18th-century English aristocrat. Definitions vary: the U.S. Department of Agriculture defines a closed sandwich as "at least 35% cooked meat and no more than 50% bread", while the British Sandwich Association describes it as "any form of bread with a filling, generally assembled cold". Savory sandwiches are the majority, though sweet types such as jam sandwiches form their own category. The *Wall Street Journal* called it Britain's "biggest contribution to gastronomy".

Mass shooting in Newtown, [[Connecticut]], on December 14, 2012, in which Adam Lanza killed 26 people, 20 of them first-grade children, before killing himself. It is the deadliest mass shooting at a K–12 school in U.S. history. A 2013 state report found that Lanza acted alone but gave no reason for his actions, and a 2014 report concluded that his mental health problems "neither caused nor led to his murderous acts". The shooting renewed national debate over gun control, and victims' families founded Sandy Hook Promise and Moms Demand Action. [[Alex Jones]] promoted hoax conspiracy theories about the attack and was later ordered to pay victims' families nearly $1.5 billion in defamation damages.

Underground pipe or tunnel system that carries sewage from buildings, but not stormwater, to a [[Sewage treatment|treatment plant]]. Most sanitary sewers are gravity sewers, typically much smaller in diameter than combined sewers, which also carry urban runoff. Separating stormwater avoids the combined sewer overflows that occur when runoff from heavy rain exceeds the capacity of treatment plants. Manholes provide access for inspection and maintenance. Where land lies lower than the treatment plant, pumped force mains or lift stations raise sewage to a higher elevation. Backups of raw sewage can occur when stormwater or [[Groundwater|groundwater]] enters through leaking joints or defective pipes in aging infrastructure. London's sewer network, completed in the 1860s under engineer Joseph Bazalgette, is a pioneering model that separated sewage from stormwater.

State in southern [[Brazil]], bordered by Paraná, Rio Grande do Sul, the [[Atlantic Ocean]] and the Argentine province of Misiones. Its population was 7.6 million in 2022, and its capital is Florianópolis. Separated from São Paulo in 1738, it is one of Brazil's oldest states. Much of its terrain is mountainous, with 52% of the territory above 600 metres. It has the lowest rates of homicide, illiteracy and poverty in the country, the third-highest [[Human Development Index]], and the least economic inequality among Brazilian states. Immigrants from the [[Azores]], Italy, Germany and other European countries shaped its population.

Legendary figure of Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts on Christmas Eve, with elves making the presents in his workshop and flying reindeer pulling his sleigh. The figure derives from Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century Greek Christian bishop known for secret gift-giving and patron saint of children. In 1087 merchants from [[Bari]] took most of his bones from Myra to Italy. The modern image originated in the United States in the 19th century, after Dutch settlers brought the legend of Sinterklaas to New Amsterdam. The 1823 poem "A Visit from St. Nicholas" established the sleigh, the reindeer and the chimney arrival. Santa is typically depicted as a portly, jolly, white-bearded man in a red coat with white fur trim.

City and capital of [[Tenerife]], and one of two capitals of the [[Canary Islands]], with 211,436 residents in 2024. It is the second-largest city in the islands. From 1833 until 1927 it was the sole capital of the archipelago. Its harbor is one of Spain's busiest and a stopover for cruise ships linking Europe, Africa and the Americas. The city hosts the Parliament of the Canary Islands. Its [[Carnival]] is among the largest in the world, and the Auditorio de Tenerife is considered one of the greatest examples of contemporary architecture.

Largest city in [[Bolivia]] and capital of the Santa Cruz department, situated on the Pirai River in the eastern tropical lowlands. Its metropolitan region is the most populous urban agglomeration in Bolivia, with an estimated 2.4 million people in 2020. Ñuflo de Chavez founded the city on February 26, 1561, about 220 km (137 mi) east of its present site, and it was moved several times before settling on the Pirai River in the late 16th century. It remained a small outpost until agrarian and land reforms after the mid-20th century triggered rapid growth. The city produces nearly 35% of Bolivia's gross domestic product and receives over 40% of all foreign direct investment in the country. Its low elevation in the Amazon basin gives it a tropical climate, unlike the far higher [[La Paz]].

Capital city of [[New Mexico]], United States (pop., 2020: 87,505), and the oldest state capital in the country. Founded in 1610 as the capital of Nuevo México, a province of [[New Spain]], it was also the earliest European settlement west of the Mississippi River. Its name means "Holy Faith". At 6,998 feet (2,133 m) it has the highest elevation of any U.S. state capital. It was named territorial capital in 1851 and became state capital in 1912. In 2005 it became the first U.S. city inducted into the [[UNESCO]] Creative Cities Network. Its adobe-style Pueblo Revival and Territorial Revival architecture is largely preserved and protected.

Spanish neuroscientist, pathologist and histologist who pioneered modern neuroscience. He shared the 1906 [[Nobel Prize]] in Physiology or Medicine with Camillo Golgi, becoming the first Spaniard to win a scientific Nobel Prize. He improved Golgi's staining method, which darkens a subset of neurons while leaving surrounding cells transparent, and used it to study the [[Central nervous system|central nervous system]]. Hundreds of his drawings of the tree-like growth of brain cells are still used for teaching. He held professorships at Zaragoza, Valencia, [[Barcelona]] and [[Madrid]], and in 1899 he directed the Instituto Nacional de Higiene. His major work is *Texture of the Nervous System of Man and the Vertebrates* (1899–1904).

Capital and largest city of [[Chile]], in the Central Valley between the Andes and the Chilean Coastal Range. Founded by the conquistador Pedro de Valdivia on February 12, 1541, it anchors a metropolitan region with more than forty communes that holds over a third of the national population and about 45% of Chile's GDP. The city houses the presidential palace and the main organs of the executive and judiciary, but the National Congress meets primarily in nearby [[Valparaíso]]. Its business district is dominated by Gran Torre Santiago, the tallest building in [[South America]]. The enclosed valley contributes to chronic [[Air pollution|air pollution]] and winter smog. One of Latin America's most extensive metro systems serves the city.

Capital and largest city of the [[Dominican Republic]], on the southern coast of [[Hispaniola]] at the mouth of the Ozama River. Founded in 1496 by the Spanish Empire, it is the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas and the first seat of Spanish colonial rule in the New World. It has the first university, cathedral, castle, monastery and fortress built in the New World, and its Colonial Zone is a [[World Heritage Site]] designated by [[UNESCO]]. From 1936 to 1961 it was called Ciudad Trujillo, after the dictator [[Rafael Trujillo]], and it reverted to its original name after his assassination. It is the largest metropolitan area in the [[Caribbean]], with 4,274,651 residents in Greater Santo Domingo as of 2022.
